title: P0: lathe threads are always cut left-hand (passes run +Z under M3; no hand parameter; posts drop the arc sense)

labels.name: P0
labels.description: Safety or crash: wrong output, gouge, data loss

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Found while building a PathPilot Hub kit for PR #626, then confirmed on upstream/main (66791aa6) with the Fanuc Lathe post.

**Today:**
- **No hand parameter:** there is no thread hand or feed direction anywhere: `ThreadParams` (`crates/motion/src/turning/thread.rs:64-78`), `OpParams::Threading` (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:2292-2304`), and the turning tool (no orientation).
- **The engine always cuts toward +Z:** passes run from the lowest station upward (`thread.rs:229-247`, `push_arc(..., true)`), and `Frame::about` forces the axis up (`profile.rs:66`), so every thread runs away from the chuck.
- **The posts drop the hand:** the CL's arc sense (ccw) describes a right-hand helix, but `fanuc-lathe.cps` `threadHalfTurn` (~l.498-517) throws it away and writes `G32 Z… F<lead>` under `M03` ("M03 always: the stream carries no spindle sense", l.61). M3 while feeding toward +Z (away from the chuck) cuts a **left-hand** thread.
- **Baked into the golden:** `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/thread_g76.nc` (M03, start Z8, `G76 … Z14`).
- **Nothing catches it:** the thread verdict judges only the meridian, so a left-hand thread on a part drawn right-hand passes silently. That is wrong output by the Prime Directive.

**Expected:**
1. **Hand parameter:** Threading carries a `hand` (RH default) and possibly a feed direction (toward or away from the chuck).
2. **Engine:** the default cut is toward the chuck (start at the top station, descend, arcs `ccw=false`), and the `ThreadCycle` record carries the hand.
3. **Posts:** every lathe post (Fanuc Lathe, the PathPilot lathe post in #626) derives the hand from the arc sense plus the Z direction and writes M03 when it matches, otherwise M04 (or refuses by name). The hand is never dropped.
4. **Goldens:** `thread_g76.nc` and the G32/G33 goldens are regenerated.

**Done means:** an RH external thread posts toward the chuck under M3 on both lathe posts; an LH thread posts M4 or the opposite direction; tests pin hand × spindle × Z direction.

Reference pending: the contributor is posting a PathPilot conversational **external** 8-32 thread (8L Hub) showing the Z direction PathPilot's G76 uses for an RH OD thread. It is syntax reference only.

Related: #626, #612.
